translations.title: The cita
translations.text:
You esperaré this night, Señor mine,

in the siniestra soledad of the soul:

in the morada antigua

where the love is lastimó the alas;

for cuyos largos corredores gime

the ausencia of your voice and tus words.


In the fosco recinto,

hondamente cavado,

where jamás the antorcha of the risa,

jamás the limpia desnudez of the llanto,

ni the atmósfera of the verso

the ecos agitaron.


There you esperaré, porque this night

not I have another morada;

to it largo of the húmedo road

all the puertas encontré cerradas,

and in the shadow tenaz perdí your huella

–the senda of your huerto and of your parra–.


¡Oh Suavísimo, come! Come, aunque encuentres

apagadas the lámparas nupciales,

aunque the voraz silencio

the roce niegue of your planta suave,

aunque your faz is esconda in the tinieblas,

aunque your beso and your word callen,

and mis miradas tendidas in the shadow

not acierten to tocarte.


You esperaré in the recinto misterioso

where in pain my mother me engendrara:

there not in the festines

is coloran the pálidas guirnaldas

ni the vino moja the encendido labio,

ni vuelan the words,

ni the antorchas brillan

enrojeciendo to the grito of the flautas:

there a largo silencio…

and a hambre oscura that your paso guarda.


Vendrás, Love… the night

all is of presagios erizada:

a pájaro without vos gime in the viento,

a inmenso love abrasa the soul.


Only I have aquel tálamos sombrío

that is ha of iluminar with your mirada,

but furtivamente

vendrás to él and dormiré in tus brazos

bajo the night to the heart amarga.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Romance: More of a ley has Love
translations.text:
More of a ley has Love
        hecha for the that not guarda,
        and of glorias that promete
        breve plazo desengaña.


        The that tenebrosa night
        pasó prometida clear
        muchos me prestó luceros
        for ver light that me falta.


        Cuántas the not fijo norte
        me hizo ver luminarias,
        tenebrosas for mí,
        puesto the sun of my esperanza;


        in cuyas dudosas sombras,
        not injusta queja acompaña
        of the deidad more dormida
        the ansia more desvelada.


        Así pasé of a olvido
        night in mal that tarde pasa,
        prestando papel the viento
        to quejas that to the viento daba.


        A prometida puerta,
        with mil lágrimas bañada,
        resistió of mis suspiros
        and of mis ansias the llama.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To a mujer that ponía the cuernos to the conde
translations.text:
Letra:


        Lágrimas of embuste
        more me endurecen,
        pues regados with ellas
        mis cuernos crecen.


        Glosa:


        Niña of the negro cabello
        and of muchos corazones,
        lloras the cuernos that pones,
        here you caigan in ello.


        Quieres that vuelva my cuello
        to the yugo of tus engaños,
        when me avisan mis daños
        and desengaños me ofrecen,
        that with lágrimas falsas
        mis cuernos crecen.


        Viví a time enamorado,
        mas already without culpa or castigo,
        cuanto escribo and cuanto digo
        is efecto recatado;
        that a cuerno ratificado
        with embustes, and of his dueño,
        dará that sentir to a leño,
        that lágrimas not merecen
        when riegan cuerno,
        mis cuernos crecen.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Romance satírico to the cazuela of the comedia
translations.text:
In the cazuela of the mundo
        all somos pepitoria,
        mas in the of the comedia
        it are the mujeres solas.
        More without gusto the cocinero
        le has the tardes all:
        who it ha probado it dice,
        who not it sabe, not it oiga.


        Porque si here are enteras,
        are the cabezas the mozas,
        and the viejas the costillas,
        nada carne and all costras;


        the flacas are the alones,
        mucho hueso in carne poca,
        and in his sudor derretidas
        are the manteca the gordas.


        The pescuezos desvaídos
        are the very largas and angostas;
        the pimienta the taimadas,
        and the mollejas the bobas;


        the feas that is aderezan
        are especias that sazonan,
        for sí solas desabridas
        and aderezadas, gustosas.


        The sangre cuajada are
        all the necias hermosas,
        and in be a manjar of the limbo
        -ni bien pena, ni bien gloria-
        the afeitadas are salsa
        adonde cualquiera moja.


        With perejiles the unas
        and with mostazas the all,
        in the portero apretador,
        for dar fin to the historia,
        is the cucharón of palo
        porque the revuelve to all.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Glosa
translations.text:
A new jinete vi
        of the tribu of Zabulón,
        not sabe of garrochón,
        of lanza and esponja sí.


        When to the monarca español
        recibe alegre Castilla,
        in his poderosa silla
        cuya águila pudo to the sun,
        be the octava maravilla
        to the plaza that atendí,
        según his be, to Dios vi,
        that was the esfera corintia,
        not me engañando the pinta
        a new jinete vi.


        Never in África lidió
        contra moros of Alá veces,
        ni cual Aníbal perdió
        the ojo when is vio
        over the Alpes franceses;
        mas of the torrente cedrón,
        vino después of Nerón
        for the incendio descrito,
        and is según is ha hallado escrito
        of the tribu of Zabulón.


        Éste, pues, desvanecido,
        porque the time le prestó,
        desque with pluma is vio,
        quiso be tan atrevido
        that his propio be negó;
        and subido in a frisón,
        without verse as pavón,
        quiso dar his pavonada,
        and aunque ha entrado estocada,
        not sabe of garrachón.


        Of the ganancia and usura
        sabe tanto that me espanto,
        as not ha robado cuanto
        the sun descubrir procura,
        that the earth encubre tanto;
        but not ha faltado there
        the natural of rabí
        that luego not le dijese
        that in garrochón not entendiese
        of lanza and of esponja sí.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To a borracho
translations.text:
Entró to hacer the razón
        Gil Toribio in the taberna,
        and in vez of hacer the razón
        Toribio quedó without ella.


        Was the divino Toribio
        a ángel in the pureza,
        and in be of espíritu puro
        is divino for esencia.


        Cual ángel cayó Toribio,
        that, aunque of vino, humos eran,
        and así luego it derriban
        humos contra the cabeza.


        Así that cayó Toribio,
        already for demonio is cuenta;
        and is the Toribio tan diablo
        that until the paredes tienta.


        The eyes has enramados
        Toribio, and is cosa cierta
        that the ramo of the eyes dice
        that there is allá dentro taberna.


        Of seda estaba vestido
        -that there is monas that visten seda-,
        and aunque is quedó vestido,
        not there is duda that in cueros queda.


        Their eyes vasos of vidrio
        for of fuera vino enseñan,
        and aunque estén encarnizados,
        more cuero that carne muestran.


        A mal le dejó of gota
        jarro that without gota queda,
        that otros renquean for gota
        and él for azumbres renquea.


        And as in cueros nació
        and in cueros morir espera,
        for more conformidad
        in cueros vivir desea.


        Always tuvo soul devota,
        always to it that Dios enseña
        humilde his pecho inclina,
        the medida it gobierna.


        Aborreció the water in life,
        and in the death is cosa cierta
        that for morir in paz
        is reconcilió with ella.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To the fin of the batalla...
translations.text:
To the fin of the batalla,

and muerto the combatiente, vino hacia él a hombre

and le dijo: «¡Not mueras, you amo tanto!»

But the cadáver ¡ay! siguió muriendo.


Is le acercaron dos and repitiéronle:

«¡Not nos dejes! ¡Valor! ¡Vuelve to the life!»

But the cadáver ¡ay! siguió muriendo.


Acudieron to él veinte, cien, mil, quinientos mil,

clamando «¡Tanto love and not poder nada contra the death!»

But the cadáver ¡ay! siguió muriendo.


Le rodearon millones of individuos,

with a ruego común: «¡Quédate hermano!»

But the cadáver ¡ay! siguió muriendo.


Entonces all the hombres of the earth

le rodearon; les vio the cadáver sad, emocionado;

incorporose lentamente,

abrazó to the primer hombre; echose to andar…
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: To my hermano Miguel
translations.text:
Hermano, today estoy in the poyo of the house,

where nos haces a falta without fondo!

Me acuerdo that jugábamos this hora, and that mamá

nos acariciaba: «But, hijos…»


Ahora I me escondo,

as antes, all estas oraciones

vespertinas, and espero that you not des conmigo.

For the sala, the zaguán, the corredores,

después, you ocultas you, and I not doy contigo.

Me acuerdo that nos hacíamos llorar,

hermano, in aquel juego.


Miguel, you you escondiste

a night of agosto, to the alborear;

but, in vez of ocultarte riendo, estabas sad.

And your gemelo heart of esas tardes

extintas is ha aburrido of not encontrarte. And already

cae shadow in the soul.


Oye, hermano, not tardes

in salir. Bueno? Puede inquietarse mamá.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XXXIX - Quién ha encendido fósforo!
translations.text:
Quién ha encendido fósforo!
                  Mésome. Sonrío
to columpio for motivo.
Sonrío aún more, si llegan all
to ver the guías without color
and to mí always in punto. What me importa.

Ni that bueno of the Sun that, to the morirse of gusto,
it desposta all for distribuirlo
between the sombras, the pródigo,
ni él me esperaría to the another banda.
Ni the demás that paran alone
entrando and saliendo.

Llama with toque of retina
the gran panadero. And pagamos in señas
curiosísimas the tibio valor innegable
horneado, trascendiente.
And tomamos the café, already tarde,
with deficiente azúcar that ha faltado,
and pan without mantequilla. What is va to hacer.

But, eso sí, the aros receñidos, barreados.
The salud va in a pie. Of frente: marchen!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema VI - The traje that vestí tomorrow
translations.text:
The traje that vestí tomorrow
not it ha lavado my lavandera:
it lavaba in their venas otilinas,
in the chorro of his heart, and today not he
of preguntarme si I dejaba
the traje turbio of injusticia.

To hora that not there is who vaya to the aguas,
in mis falsillas encañona
the lienzo for emplumar, and all the cosas
of the velador of tánto what será of mí,
all not are mías
to my lado. Quedaron of his propiedad,
fratesadas, selladas with his trigueña bondad.

And si supiera si ha of volver;
and si supiera what tomorrow entrará
to entregarme the ropas lavadas, my aquella
lavandera of the soul. That tomorrow entrará
satisfecha, capulí of obrería, dichosa
of probar that sí sabe, that sí puede ¡How Not VA To PODER!
azular and planchar all the caos.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LXXI - Serpea the sun in your hand fresca
translations.text:
Serpea the sun in your hand fresca,
and is derrama cauteloso in your curiosidad.

Cállate. Nadie sabe that estás in mí,
all entera. Cállate. Not respires. Nadie
sabe my merienda suculenta of unidad:
legión of oscuridades, amazonas of lloro.

Vanse the carros flajelados for the tarde,
and between ellos the míos, cara atrás, to the riendas
fatales of tus dedos.
Tus hands and mis hands recíprocas is tienden
polos in guardia, practicando depresiones,
and sienes and costados.

Calla también, crepúsculo futuro,
and recójete to reír in it íntimo, of this celo
of gallos ajisecos soberbiamente,
soberbiamente ennavajados
of cúpulas, of viudas mitades cerúleas.
Regocíjate, huérfano; bebe your copa of water
from the pulpería of a esquina cualquiera.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LXIV - Hitos vagarosos enamoran, from the minuto montuoso that obstetriza
translations.text:
Hitos vagarosos enamoran, from the minuto montuoso that obstetriza
and fécha the amotinados nichos of the atmósfera.

Verde is the heart of tánto esperar, and in the canal of Panamá
¡hablo with vosotras, mitades, bases, cúspides! retoñan the peldaños,
pasos that suben,
pasos that baja-
n.
And I that pervivo,
and I that sé plantarme.

Oh valle without altura mother, where all duerme horrible mediatinta,
without ríos frescos, without entradas of love. Oh voces and ciudades, that pasan
cabalgando in a dedo tendido that señala to calva Unidad. Mientras
pasan, of mucho in mucho, gañanes of gran costado sabio, detrás of the
tres tardas dimensiones.

Today                                             Tomorrow                                             Ayer
      (Not, hombre!)
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: ¡Cuídate, España, of your propia España!
translations.text:
¡Cuídate, España, of your propia España!

¡Cuídate of the hoz without the martillo,

cuídate of the martillo without the hoz!

¡Cuídate of the víctima to pesar suyo,

of the verdugo to pesar suyo

and of the indiferente to pesar suyo!

¡Cuídate of the that, antes of that cante the gallo,

negárate tres veces,

and of the that you negó, después, tres veces!

¡Cuídate of the calaveras without the tibias,

and of the tibias without the calaveras!

¡Cuídate of the nuevos poderosos!

¡Cuídate of the that come tus cadáveres,

of the that devora muertos to tus vivos!

¡Cuídate of the leal ciento for ciento!

¡Cuídate of the sky more acá of the air

and cuídate of the air more allá of the sky!

¡Cuídate of the that you aman!

¡Cuídate of tus héroes!

¡Cuídate of tus muertos!

¡Cuídate of the República!

¡Cuídate of the futuro!…
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Verano
translations.text:
Verano, already me voy. And me dan pena

the manitas sumisas of tus tardes.

Llegas devotamente; llegas old;

and already not encontrarás in my soul to nadie.


Verano! and pasarás for mis balcones

with gran rosario of amatistas and oros,

as a obispo sad that llegara

of lejos to buscar and bendecir

the rotos aros of unos muertos novios.


Verano, already me voy. Allá, in setiembre

I have a rosa that you encargo mucho;

the regarás of water bendita all

the días of pecado and of sepulcro.


Si to fuerza of llorar the mausoleo,

with light of fe his mármol aletea,

levanta in alto your responso, and pide

to Dios that siga for always muerta.

All ha of be already tarde;

and you not encontrarás in my soul to nadie.


Already not llores, Verano! In aquel surco

muere a rosa that renace mucho…
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LXX - All sonríen of the desgaire with that voyme to fondo, celular of comer
translations.text:
All sonríen of the desgaire with that voyme to fondo, celular of comer
bien and bien beber.

The soles andan without yantar? Or there is who
les da granos as to pajarillos? Francamente,
I not sé of esto casi nada.

Oh piedra, almohada bienfaciente to the fin. Amémonos os vivos to the
vivos, that to the buenas cosas muertas será después. Cuánto tenemos that
quererlas
and estrecharlas, cuánto. Amemos the actualidades, that always not
estaremos as estamos.
That interinos Barrancos not there is in the esenciales cementerios.

The porteo va in the alfar, to pico. The jornada nos da in the cogollo, with his
docena of escaleras, escala das, in horizontizante frustración of pies,
for pávidas sandalias vacantes.

And temblamos avanzar the paso, that not sabemos si damos with the
péndulo, or already it hemos cruzado.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XLII - Esperaos. Already os voy to narrar
translations.text:
Esperaos. Already os voy to narrar
all. Esperaos sossiegue
this pain of cabeza. Esperaos.

¿Dónde os habéis dejado vosotros
that not hacéis falta jamás?

Nadie makes falta! Very bien.

Rosa, entra of the último piso.
Estoy niño. And another vez rosa:
ni sabes to dónde voy.

¿Aspa the estrella of the death?
Or are extrañas máquinas cosedoras
dentro of the costado izquierdo.
Esperaos another momento.

Not nos ha visto nadie. Pura
búscate the talle.
¡To dónde is han saltado tus eyes!

Penetra reencarnada in the salones
of ponentino cristal. Suena
música exacta casi lástima.

Me siento mejor. Without fiebre, and ferviente.
Primavera. Perú. Abro the eyes.
Ave! Not salgas. Dios, as si sospechase
algún flujo without reflujo ay.

Paletada facial, resbala the telón
cabe the conchas.
      Acrisis. Tilia, acuéstate.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XXII - Is posible me persigan until cuatro
translations.text:
Is posible me persigan until cuatro
magistrados vuelto. Is posible me juzguen pedro.
¡Cuatro humanidades justas juntas!
Don Juan Jacobo is in hacerio,
and the burlas le tiran of his soledad,
as to a tonto. Bien hecho.

Farol rotoso, the day induce to darle algo,
and pende
to modo of asterisco that is mendiga
to sí propio quizás what enmendaturas.

Ahora that chirapa tan bonito
in this paz of a sola línea,
here me you have,
here me you have, of who I penda,
for that sacies mis esquinas.
And si, éstas colmadas,
you derramases of mayor bondad,
sacaré of where not haya,
forjaré of locura otros posillos,
insaciables ganas
of nivel and love.

Si pues always salimos to the encuentro
of cuanto entra for another lado,
ahora, chirapado eterno and all,
heme, of who I penda,
estoy of filo todavía. Heme!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Comunión
translations.text:
Linda Regia! Tus venas are fermentos

of my not be antiguo and of the champaña

negro of my vivir!


Your cabello is the ignota raicilla

of the árbol of my vid.

Your cabello is the hilacha of a mitra

of ensueño that perdí!


Your body is the espumante escaramuza

of a rosado Jordán;

and ondea, as a látigo beatífico

that humillara to the víbora of the mal!


Tus brazos dan the sed of it infinito,

with their castas hespérides of light,

cual dos blancos caminos redentores,

dos arranques murientes of a cruz.

And are plasmados in the sangre invicta

of my imposible azul!


Tus pies are dos heráldicas alondras

that eternamente llegan of my ayer!

Linda Regia! Tus pies are the dos lágrimas

that to the bajar of the Espíritu ahogué,

a Domingo of Ramos that entré to the Mundo,

already lejos for always of Belén!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Varios días the air, compañeros
translations.text:
Varios días the air, compañeros,
muchos días the viento cambia of air,
the terreno, of filo,
of nivel the fusil republicano.
Varios días España is española.

Varios días the mal
moviliza their órbitas, is abstiene,
paraliza their eyes escuchándolos.
Varios días orando with sudor desnudo,
the milícianos cuélganse of the hombre.
Varios días, the mundo, camarada,
the mundo is español until the death.

Varios días ha muerto here the disparo
and ha muerto the body in his papel of espíritu
and the soul is already nuestra soul, compañeros.
Varios días the sky,
éste, the of the day, the of the pata enorme.

Varios días, Gijón;
muchos días, Gijón;
mucho time, Gijón;
mucha earth, Gijón;
mucho hombre, Gijón;
and mucho dios, Gijón,
muchísimas Españas ¡ay! Gijón.

Camaradas,
varios días the viento cambia of air.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The heraldos negros
translations.text:
There is golpes in the life, tan fuertes… ¡I not sé!

Golpes as of the odio of Dios; as si ante ellos,

the resaca of all it sufrido

is empozara in the soul… ¡I not sé!


Are pocos; but are… Abren zanjas oscuras

in the rostro more fiero and in the lomo more fuerte.

Serán tal vez the potros of bárbaros atilas;

or the heraldos negros that nos manda the Death.


Are the caídas hondas of the Cristos of the soul

of alguna fe adorable that the Destino blasfema.

Esos golpes sangrientos are the crepitaciones

of algún pan that in the puerta of the horno is nos quema.


And the hombre… Pobre… ¡pobre! Vuelve the eyes,

as when for over the hombro nos llama a palmada;

vuelve the eyes locos, and all it vivido is empoza,

as charco of culpa, in the mirada.


There is golpes in the life, tan fuertes… ¡I not sé!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XVIII - Oh the cuatro paredes of the celda
translations.text:
Oh the cuatro paredes of the celda.
Ah the cuatro paredes albicantes
that without remedio dan to the mismo número.

Criadero of nervios, mala brecha,
for their cuatro rincones how arranca
the diarias aherrojadas extremidades.

Amorosa llavera of innumerables llaves,
si estuvieras here, si vieras until
what hora are cuatro estas paredes.
Contra ellas seríamos contigo, the dos,
more dos that never. And ni lloraras,
di, libertadora!

Ah the paredes of the celda.
Of ellas me duele entretanto, more
the dos largas that tienen this night
algo of madres that already muertas
llevan for bromurados declives,
to a niño of the hand each a.

And only I me voy quedando,
with the diestra, that makes for ambas hands,
in alto, in busca of terciario brazo
that ha of pupilar, between my dónde and my cuándo,
this mayoría inválida of hombre.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The pasos lejanos
translations.text:
My father duerme. His semblante augusto
        figura a apacible heart;
        is ahora tan dulce…
        si there is algo in él of amargo, seré I.


        There is soledad in the hogar; is reza;
        and not there is noticias of the hijos today.
        My father is despierta, ausculta
        the huida to Egipto, the restañante adiós.


        Is ahora tan cerca;
        si there is algo in él of lejos, seré I.
        And my mother pasea allá in the huertos,
        saboreando a sabor already without sabor.
        Is ahora tan suave,
        tan ala, tan salida, tan love.


        There is soledad in the hogar without bulla,
        without noticias, without verde, without niñez.
        And si there is algo quebrado in this tarde,
        and that baja and that cruje,
        are dos viejos caminos blancos, curvos.
        For ellos va my heart to pie.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Small responso to a héroe of the República
translations.text:
A libro quedó to the borde of his cintura muerta,
a libro retoñaba of his cadáver muerto.
Is llevaron to the héroe,
and corpórea and aciaga entró his mouth in nuestro aliento;
sudamos all, the hombligo to cuestas;
caminantes the lunas nos seguían;
también sudaba of tristeza the muerto.

And a libro, in the batalla of Toledo,
a libro, atrás a libro, arriba a libro, retoñaba of the cadáver.

Poesía of the pómulo morado, between the decirlo
and the callarlo,
poesía in the carta moral that acompañara
to his heart.
Quedóse the libro and nada more, that not there is
insectos in the tumba,
and quedó to the borde (le his manga, the air remojándose
and haciéndose gaseoso, infinito.

All sudamos, the ombligo to cuestas,
también sudaba of tristeza the muerto
and a libro, I it vi sentidamente,
a libro, atrás a libro, arriba a libro
retoño of the cadáver ex abrupto.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LVI - All the días amanezco to ciegas
translations.text:
All the días amanezco to ciegas
to trabajar for vivir; and tomo the desayuno,
without probar ni gota of él, all the mañanas.
Without saber si he logrado, or more never,
algo that brinca of the sabor
or is only heart and that already vuelto, lamentará
until dónde esto is it menos.

The niño crecería ahito of felicidad
                                       oh albas,
ante the pesar of the padres of not poder dejarnos
of arrancar of their sueños of love to this mundo;
ante ellos that, as Dios, of tanto love
is comprendieron until creadores
and nos quisieron until hacernos daño.

Flecos of invisible trama,
dientes that huronean from the neutra emoción,
                                       pilares
libres of base and coronación,
in the gran mouth that ha perdido the habla.

Fósforo and fósforo in the oscuridad,
lágrima and lágrima in the polvareda.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XLVII - Ciliado arrecife where nací
translations.text:
Ciliado arrecife where nací,
según refieren cronicones and pliegos
of labios familiares historiados
in segunda gracia.

Ciliado archipiélago, you desislas to fondo,
                                                      to fondo, archipiélago mine!
Duras todavía the articulaciones
to the road, as when nos instan,
and nosotros not cedemos for nada.

To the ver the párpados cerrados,
implumes mayorcitos, devorando azules bombones,
is carcajean pericotes viejos.
The párpados cerrados, correo si, when nacemos,
always not fuese time todavía.

Is va the altar, the cirio for
that not le pasase nada to my mother,
and for mí that sería with the años, si Dios
quería, Obispo, Papa, Santo, or talvez
only a columnario pain of cabeza.

And the manitas that is abarquillan
asiéndose of algo flotante,
to not querer quedarse.
And siendo already the 1.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema L - The cancerbero cuatro veces
translations.text:
The cancerbero cuatro veces
to the day maneja his candado, abriéndonos
cerrándonos the esternones, in guiños
that entendemos perfectamente.

With the fundillos lelos melancólicos,
amuchachado of trascendental desaliño,
parado, is adorable the pobre old.
Chancea with the presos, until the tope
the puños in the ingles. And until mojarrilla
les roe algún mendrugo; but always
cumpliendo his deber.

For between the barrotes pone the punto
fiscal, inadvertido, izándose in the falangita
of the meñique,
to the pista of it that hablo,
it that as,
it that dream.
Quiere the corvino already not hayan adentros,
and how nos duele esto that quiere the cancerbero.

For a sistema of relojería, juega
the old inminente, pitagórico!
to it ancho of the aortas. And only
of tarde in night, with night
soslaya alguna his excepción of metal.
But, naturalmente,
always cumpliendo his deber.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XXV - Alfan alfiles to adherirse
translations.text:
Alfan alfiles to adherirse
to the junturas, to the fondo, to the testuces,
to the sobrelecho of the numeradores to pie.
Alfiles and cadillos of lupinas parvas.

To the rebufar the socaire of each caravela
deshilada without ameracanizar,
ceden the estevas in espasmo of infortunio,
with pulso párvulo mal habituado
to sonarse in the dorso of the muñeca.
And the more aguda tiplisonancia
is tonsura and apeálase, and largamente
is ennazala hacia carámbanos
of lástima infinita.

Soberbios lomos resoplan
to the portar, pendientes of mustios petrales
the escarapelas with their siete colores
bajo cero, from the islas guaneras
until the islas guaneras.
Tal the escarzos to the intemperie of pobre
fe.
Tal the time of the rondas. Tal the of the rodeo
for the planos futuros,
when innánima grifalda relata only
fallidas callandas cruzadas.

Vienen entonces alfiles to adherirse
until in the puertas falsas and in the borradores.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The mendigos pelean for España
translations.text:
The mendigos pelean for España,
mendigando in París, in Roma, in Praga
and refrendando así, with hand gótica, rogante,
the pies of the Apóstoles, in Londres, in New York, in Méjico.
The pordioseros luchan suplicando infernalmente
to Dios For Santander,
the lid in that already nadie is derrotado.
To the sufrimiento antiguo
danse, encarnízanse in llorar plomo social
to the pie of the individuo,
and atacan to gemidos, the mendigos,
matando with tan alone be mendigos.

Ruegos of infantería,
in that the arma ruega of the metal for arriba,
and ruega the ira, more acá of the pólvora iracunda.
Tácitos escuadrones that disparan,
with cadencia mortal, his mansedumbre,
from a umbral, from sí mismos, ¡ay! from sí mismos.
Potenciales guerreros
without calcetines to the calzar the trueno,
satánicos, numéricos,
arrastrando their títulos of fuerza,
migaja to the cinto,
fusil doble calibre: sangre and sangre.
¡The poeta saluda to the sufrimiento armado!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema XL - Quién nos hubiera dicho that in domingo
translations.text:
Quién nos hubiera dicho that in domingo
así, over arácnidas cuestas
is encabritaría the shadow of puro frontal.
(A molusco ataca yermos eyes encallados,
to razón of dos or more posibilidades tantálicas
contra medio estertor of sangre remordida).

Entonces, ni the propio revés of the pantalla
deshabitado enjugaría the arterias
trasdoseadas of dobles todavías.
As si nos hubiesen dejado salir! As
si not estuviésemos embrazados always
to the dos flancos diarios of the fatalidad!
      And cuánto nos habríamos ofendido.
And aún it that nos habríamos enojado and peleado
and amistado another vez
and another vez.

Quién hubiera pensado in tal domingo,
when, to rastras, seis codos lamen
of this manera, hueras yemas lunesentes.

Habríamos sacado contra él, of bajo
of the dos alas of the Love,
lustrales plumas terceras, puñales,
nuevos pasajes of papel of oriente.
For today that probamos si aún vivimos,
casi a frente not more.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Absoluta
translations.text:
Color of ropa antigua. A julio to shadow,
        and a agosto recién segado. And a
        hand of water that injertó in the pino
        resinoso of a tedio malas frutas.


        Ahora that has anclado, oscura ropa,
        tornas rociada of a suntuoso olor
        to time, to abreviación… And he cantado
        the proclive festín that is volcó.


        Mas ¿not puedes, Señor, contra the death,
        contra the límite, contra it that acaba?
        ¡Ay, the llaga in color of ropa antigua,
        how is entreabre and huele to miel quemada!


        ¡Oh unidad excelsa! ¡Oh it that is uno for all!
        ¡Love contra the espacio and contra the time!
        A latido único of heart;
        a alone ritmo: ¡Dios!


        And to the encogerse of hombros the linderos
        in a bronco desdén irreductible,
        there is a riego of sierpes
        in the doncella plenitud of the 1.
        ¡A arruga, a shadow!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LXVIII - Estamos to catorce of Julio
translations.text:
Estamos to catorce of Julio.
Are the cinco of the tarde. Llueve in all
a tercera esquina of papel secante.
And llueve more of abajo ay for arriba.

Dos lagunas the hands avanzan
of diez in fondo,
from a martes cenagoso that ha seis días
is in the lagrimales helado.

Is ha degollado a semana
with the more agudas caídas; hase hecho
all it that puede hacer miserable genial
in gran taberna without rieles. Ahora estamos
bien, with this rain that nos lava
and nos alegra and nos makes gracia suave.

Hemos to peso bruto caminado, and, of a alone
                              desafío,
blanqueó nuestra pureza of animales.
And preguntamos for the eterno love,
for the encuentro absoluto,
for cuanto pasa of here for allá.
And respondimos from dónde the míos not are the tuyos
from what hora the bordón, to the be portado,
sustenta and not is sustentado. (Neto.)

And was negro, colgado in a rincón,
without proferir ni jota, my paletó,
to
t
or
d
to
s
t
To
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Romería
translations.text:
Pasamos juntos. The dream
        lame nuestros pies what dulce;
        and all is desplaza in pálidas
        renunciaciones without dulce.


        Pasamos juntos. The muertas
        almas, the that, cual nosotros,
        cruzaron for the love,
        with enfermos pasos ópalos,
        salen in their lutos rígidos
        and is ondulan in nosotros.
        Amada, let us go to the borde
        frágil of a montón of earth.
        Va in aceite ungida the ala,
        and in pureza. But a golpe,
        to the caer I not sé dónde,
        afila of each lágrima
        a diente hostil.


        And a soldado, a gran soldado,
        heridas for charreteras,
        is anima in the tarde heroica,
        and to their pies muestra between risas,
        as a gualdrapa horrenda,
        the cerebro of the Life.


        Pasamos juntos, very juntos,
        invicta Light, paso enfermo;
        pasamos juntos the lilas
        mostazas of a cementerio.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Where never llegaremos
translations.text:
Where, aún without nuestro pie
        llegase to dar for a instante
        será, in verdad, as not estarse.


        Is that a sitio that is ve
        to each rato in this life,
        andando, andando of uno in fila.


        More acá of mí mismo and of
        my par of yemas, it he entrevisto
        always lejos of the destinos.


        Already podéis iros to pie
        or to puro sentimiento in pelo,
        that to él not arriban ni the sellos.


        The horizonte color té
        is muere for colonizarle
        for his gran Cualquieraparte.


        Mas the lugar that I me sé,
        in this mundo, nada menos,
        hombreado va with the reversos.


        -Cerrad aquella puerta that
        is entreabierta in the entrañas
        of that espejo. -¿This? – Not; his hermana.


        -Not is puede cerrar. Not is
        puede llegar never to aquel sitio
        -do van in rama the pestillos.


        Tal is the lugar that I me sé.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema III - The personas mayores
translations.text:
The personas mayores
¿to what hora volverán?
Da the seis the ciego Santiago,
and already is very oscuro.

Mother dijo that not demoraría.

Aguedita, Nativa, Miguel,
cuidado with ir for ahí, for where
acaban of pasar gangueando their memorias
dobladoras penas,
hacia the silencioso corral, and for where
the gallinas that is are acostando todavía,
is han espantado tanto.
Mejor estemos here not more.
Mother dijo that not demoraría.

Already not tengamos pena. Let us go viendo
the barcos ¡the mine is more bonito of all!
with the cuales jugamos all the santo day,
without pelearnos, as debe of be:
han quedado in the pozo of water, listos,
fletados of dulces for tomorrow.

Aguardemos así, obedientes and without more
remedio, the vuelta, the desagravio
of the mayores always delanteros
dejándonos in house to the pequeños,
as si también nosotros not pudiésemos partir.

Aguedita, Nativa, Miguel?
Llamo, busco to the tanteo in the oscuridad.
Not me vayan to haber dejado alone,
and the único recluso sea I.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Cortejo tras the toma of Bilbao
translations.text:
Herido and muerto, hermano,
criatura veraz, republicana, are andando in his trono,
from that your espinazo cayó famosamente;
are andando, pálido, in your edad flaca and anual,
laboriosamente absorta ante the vientos.

Guerrero in ambos dolores,
siéntate to oír, acuéstate to the pie of the palo súbito,
inmediato of your trono;
voltea;
are the nuevas sábanas, extrañas;
are andando, hermano, are andando.

Han dicho “¡As! ¡Dónde!…”, expresándose
in trozos of paloma,
and in the niños suben without llorar to your polvo.
Ernesto Zúñiga, duerme with the hand puesta,
with the concepto puesto,
in descanso your paz, in paz your guerra.

Herido mortalmente of life, camarada,
camarada jinete,
camarada caballo between hombre and earth,
tus huesecillos of alto and melancólico dibujo
forman pompa española,
laureada of finísimos andrajos.

Siéntate, pues, Ernesto,
oye that are andando, here, in your trono,
from that your tobillo has canas.
¿What trono?
¡Your zapato derecho! ¡Your zapato!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LXVII - Canta cerca the verano, and ambos
translations.text:
Canta cerca the verano, and ambos
diversos erramos, to the hombro
recodos, cedros, compases unípedos,
espatarrados in the sola recta inevitable.

Canta the verano, and in aquellas paredes
endulzadas of marzo,
lloriquea, gusanea the arácnida acuarela
                                    of the melancolía.

Cuadro enmarcado of trisado anélido, cuadro
that faltó in that sitio for where
pensamos that vendría the gran espejo ausente.
Love, éste is the cuadro that faltó.

Mas, for what me esforzaría
for dorar pajilla for tal encantada aurícula,
si, to espaldas of astros queridos,
is consiente the vacío, to pesar of all.

Cuánta mother quedábase adentrada
always, in tenaz atavío of carbón, when
the cuadro faltaba, and for it that crecería
to the pie of ardua quebrada of mujer.

Así I me decía: Si vendrá aquel espejo
that of tan esperado, already pasa of cristal.
Me acababa the life, ¿for what?
Me acababa the life, for alzarnos

                                    only of espejo to espejo.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: The pan nuestro
translations.text:
Is bebe the desayuno… Húmeda earth

of cementerio huele to sangre amada.

Ciudad of invierno… The mordaz cruzada

of a carreta that arrastrar parece

a emoción of ayuno encadenada!


Is quisiera tocar all the puertas,

and preguntar for not sé quién; and luego

ver to the pobres, and, llorando quedos,

dar pedacitos of pan fresco to all.

And saquear to the ricos their viñedos

with the dos hands santas

that to a golpe of light

volaron desclavadas of the Cruz!


Pestaña matinal, not os levantéis!

¡The pan nuestro of each day dánoslo,

Señor…!


All mis huesos are ajenos;

I talvez the robé!

I vine to darme it that acaso estuvo

asignado for another;

and pienso that, si not hubiera nacido,

another pobre tomara this café!

I soy a mal ladrón… To dónde iré!


And in this hora fría, in that the earth

trasciende to polvo humano and is tan sad,

quisiera I tocar all the puertas,

and suplicar to not sé quién, perdón,

and hacerle pedacitos of pan fresco

here, in the horno of my heart…!
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LXII -  Alfombra
translations.text:
Alfombra
When vayas to the cuarto that you sabes,
entra in él, but entorna with tiento the mampara
that tánto is entreabre,
cása bien the cerrojos, for that already not puedan
volverse otras espaldas.

                          Corteza
And when salgas, di that not tardarás
to llamar to the canal that nos separa:
fuertemente cojido of a canto of your suerte,
you soy inseparable,
and me arrastras of borde of your soul.

                          Almohada
And only when hayamos muerto ¡quién sabe!
                          Oh nó. Quién sabe!
entonces nos habremos separado.
Mas si, to the cambiar the paso, me tocase to mí
the desconocida bandera, you he of esperar allá;
in the confluencia of the soplo and the hueso,
as antaño,
as antaño in the esquina of the novios
                          ponientes of the earth.

And from there you seguiré to it largo
of otros mundos, and siquiera podrán
servirte mis nós musgosos and arrecidos,
for that in ellos poses the rodillas
in the siete caídas of that cuesta infinita,
and así you duelan menos.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Redoble fúnebre to the escombros of Durango
translations.text:
Father polvo that subes of España,
Dios you salve, libere and corone,
father polvo that asciendes of the soul.

Father polvo that subes of the fire,
Dios you salve, you calce and dé your trono,
father polvo that estás in the cielos.

Father polvo, biznieto of the humo,
Dios you salve and ascienda to infinito,
father polvo, biznieto of the humo.

Father polvo in that acaban the justos,
Dios you salve and devuelva to the earth,
father polvo in that acaban the justos.

Father polvo that creces in palmas,
Dios you salve and revista of pecho,
father polvo, terror of the nada.

Father polvo, compuesto of hierro,
Dios you salve and you of forma of hombre,
father polvo that marchas ardiendo.

Father polvo, sandalia of paria,
Dios you salve and jamás you desate.

Father polvo that avientan the bárbaros,

Dios you salve and you ciña of dioses,
father polvo that escoltan the átomos.

Father polvo, sudario of the pueblo,
Dios you salve of the mal for always,
father polvo español, father nuestro.

Father polvo that vas to the futuro,
Dios you salve, you guíe and you dé alas,
father polvo that vas to the futuro.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Trilce: Poema LV - Samain diría the air is quieto and of a contenida tristeza
translations.text:
Samain diría the air is quieto and of a contenida tristeza.

Vallejo dice today the Death is soldando each lindero to
each hebra of cabello perdido, from the cubeta of a frontal,
where there is algas, toronjiles that cantan divinos almácigos in
guardia, and versos anti sépticos without dueño.

The miércoles, with uñas destronadas is abre the propias uñas
of alcanfor, e instila for polvorientos
harneros, ecos, páginas vueltas, sarros,
zumbidos of moscas
when there is muerto, and pena clear esponjosa and cierta esperanza.

A enfermo lee The Prensa, as in facistol.
Another is tendido palpitante, longirrostro,
cerca to estarlo sepulto.
And I advierto a hombro is in his sitio
todavía and casi queda listo tras of éste, the another lado.

Already the tarde pasó diez and seis veces for the subsuelo empatrullado,
and is is casi ausente
in the número of madera amarilla
of the cama that is desocupada tanto time
                                    allá .....................................
                                                                 enfrente.
translations.editorial_note: Translation staged from the supplied local text; no separate editorial review was performed.
